rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison sets Qasas’s geographic detail, family instruction, and hopeful ‘perhaps I will bring’ against Naml’s shorter, definite ‘I will bring.’
rows.anchor: لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas asks for a jadwa of fire; Naml speaks of bringing a shihab qabas.
rows.anchor: أو جذوة من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas says ‘when he reached it’ and specifies the call’s location; Naml uses ‘came to it,’ adds the blessing and glorification, and omits the place detail.
rows.anchor: نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas uses ‘an ya Musa’ and names God as Lord of the worlds; Naml directly addresses Musa and names God the Mighty, Wise.
rows.anchor: يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other contrasts include inserting versus passing the hand, two proofs versus nine signs, Qasas’s wing gesture, and Pharaoh’s people versus his elite.
rows.anchor: واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب

words: بورك من في النار ومن حولها وسبحان الله رب العالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml adds the blessing formula, absent from Qasas, because this scene is one of glorifying God.
rows.anchor: الموقف في النمل موقف تعظيم كما أسلفنا وهذا القول تعظيم لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml directly calls Musa to honor him; Qasas uses explanatory an because its scene does not carry the same honorific force.
rows.anchor: فشرفه بالنداء المباشر في حين ليس المقام كذلك في القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qasas, an is explicative: the call means ‘in words or a sign conveying this meaning,’ unlike an explicit quoted utterance; the author compares 37:104–105 and 11:46.
rows.anchor: فالأول معناه: أشرت إليه بالذهاب، بأي لفظ أو دلالة تدل على هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas’s more expansive, detailed mode suits adding an before the call.
rows.anchor: المقام في سورة القصص مقام تبسط وتفصيل فجاء بـ (أن) زيادة في التبسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weightier commission in Naml calls for a direct summons.
rows.anchor: ثقل التكليف في النمل يستدعي المباشرة في النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml’s pronoun of شأن in ‘innahu ana’ and the names al-Aziz al-Hakim add exaltation; Qasas instead says ‘inni ana Allah rabb al-alamin.’
rows.anchor: فجاء بضمير الشأن الدال على التعظيم في آية النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jadwa may or may not be a borrowed flame; the shihab qabas gives greater benefit and signals steadiness and courage. He places the ember in the fearful setting and the flame in the other setting.
rows.anchor: الجذوة قد تكون قبسا وغير قبس

rows.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes atyan as an easy coming and says maji is broader because atyan specifically implies ease.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الأصفهاني مفرقا بين الإتيان والمجيء: الإتيان مجيءٌ بسهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicons usually define the two verbs by each other, but derivatives of atā indicate ease, as in an easy road and water channels made easy.
rows.anchor: غير أنهم يذكرون في بعض تصريفات (أتى) ما يدل على السهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses jā’a for difficulty or greater hardship than atā, as in 23:27, 50:19, and 18:71, 18:74.
rows.anchor: والذي استبان لي أن القرآن الكريم يستعمل المجيء لما فيه صعوبة ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa’s Naml promise is firmer than his Qasas hope, and bringing a bright, borrowed flame is harder than bringing an ember; these make Naml’s situation more arduous.
rows.anchor: ما قطعه موسى على نفسه في النمل أصعب مما في القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml’s commission to Pharaoh and his people is broader and harder than Qasas’s commission to Pharaoh and his elite, since the people are dispersed and varied.
rows.anchor: وتبليغ القوم أوسع وأصعب من تبليغ الملأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Taha account, where Musa is sent to Pharaoh alone, says ‘ataha’; this supports the lighter verb in a less demanding setting.
rows.anchor: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Naml circumstances are harder, it uses jā’a rather than the lighter atā.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالفعل (جاء) دون (أتى) الذي هو أخف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas gives the direction and setting of the call for its detailed mode; Naml’s mode is concise.
rows.anchor: موطن القصص موطن تفصيل، وموطن النمل موطن إيجاز كما ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root d-kh-l and its derivatives occur five times in Naml, at 27:12, 18, 19, 34, and 44, but not in Qasas, which suits Naml’s use of ‘insert.’
rows.anchor: إن الفعل (دخل) ومشتقاته تكرر خمس مرات (انظر الآيات 12، 18، 19، 34، 44) في النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idkhal is narrower than suluk: suluk may mean traversing or inserting, while idkhal specifically means insertion.
rows.anchor: الإدخال أخص من السلك أو السلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suluk can be easy and effortless, as in the bee following gentle paths and water entering springs; insertion is harder and suits the difficult commission.
rows.anchor: فناسب وضع السلوك في موطن السهولة واليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suluk fits the fearful setting, whereas idkhal fits security and confidence.
rows.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع السلوك في مقام الخوف، وأن يوضع لإدخال في مقام الأمن والثقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more specific idkhal matches the specific shihab qabas; the broader suluk matches the broader jadwa.
rows.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع الإدخال وهو أخص من السلوك مع (الشهاب القبس)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas adds the wing gesture because fear recurs in that story and the surah gives a fuller account.
rows.anchor: (الرهب) هو الخوف، وهو مناسب لجو الخوف الذي تردد في القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison notes that Naml says ‘among nine signs,’ while Qasas says ‘those two proofs.’
rows.anchor: قال في النمل: "في تسعِ آياتٍ" وقال في القصص: "فذانِكَ بُرهانانِ"

words: فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired formulas track surah vocabulary: faith occurs 24 times and taqwa 7 in An‘am; faith 21 and taqwa 11 in A‘raf.
rows.anchor: الإيمان ومشتقاته ورد 24 مرة والتقوى وردت 7 مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahl repeats ‘amal ten times and never kasb; Zumar repeats kasb five times and ‘amal six, matching its wording choices.
rows.anchor: تكرر العمل 10 مرات والكسب لم يرد أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taha uses atyan more than fifteen times and maji four; Naml uses maji eight times and atyan thirteen, fitting their respective verb choices here.
rows.anchor: تكرر لفظ الإتيان أكثر من 15 مرة والمجيء 4 مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares divine-name frequencies: Baqarah has Allah 282 times and rabb 47; An‘am has rabb 53 and Allah 87, alongside different distribution of the formulas ‘Allah is Forgiving, Merciful’ and ‘your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.’
rows.anchor: تكرر لفظ الجلالة (الله) 282 مرة و (الرب) 47 مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is not a conjunction; it is the required response particle for the relative conditional alladhina, and no other particle substitutes for it.
rows.anchor: الفاء في موضعها وهي ليست حرف عطف ولكنها جواب للذين

words: لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression negates fear nominally and grief verbally, emphasizes ‘they’ for grief, and has no equivalent phrasing.
rows.anchor: نفى الخوف بالصورة الإسمية ونفى الحزن بالصورة الفعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse came while the Prophet preached after Friday prayer: a caravan arrived during a high-price, difficult year, and people left for trade rather than amusement.
rows.anchor: فجاءت العير بتجارة وكانت سنة شديدة فانفض الناس بسبب التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade comes first in the opening because it drew the people away; at the end amusement comes first because many are distracted by it, and God’s reward exceeds both.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قدّم التجارة في أول الآية (وإذا رأوا تجارة) . ثم في نهاية الآية قدّم تعالى اللهو على التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amusement is named before trade in the closing phrase as Arabic ordering rises from the lower item to the higher.
rows.anchor: فذكر الأدنى (اللهو) ثم الأعلى (التجارة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God is the best provider’ appropriately follows trade, which is a source of livelihood, rather than amusement.
rows.anchor: لأن التجارة مظنّة الرزق فوضع التجارة بجانب قوله تعالى (والله خير الرازقين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating min shows that God’s favor applies independently to amusement and trade; a single min would imply it applies only to the two together.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو قال (من اللهو والتجارة) لأفاد أن الخيرية لا تكون إلا باجتماعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 5:60, ‘worshipped the idol’ is not coordinated with apes and swine; it is a past-tense verb coordinated with ‘He made some of them,’ so a clause is coordinated with a clause.
rows.anchor: ليست معطوفة على القردة والخنازير وإنما هي فعل ماضي معطوفة على (وجعل منهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying messengers do not fear in God’s presence indirectly identifies Musa as one of them, honoring him.
rows.anchor: فألمح بذلك إلى نه منهم، وهذا تكريم وتشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ladayya suggests nearness, which adds to the honor and distinction.
rows.anchor: مشعرا بالقرب، وهو زيادة في التكريم والتشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct ‘ya Musa’ and ‘wa-alqi asaka’ omit Qasas’s an, signaling nearness in both the summons and command.
rows.anchor: فناداه من قرب وأمره من قرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers are secure in God’s presence while still fearing and revering Him greatly; the verse does not say they do not fear God.
rows.anchor: لأن المرسلين لا يخافون بحضرته، ولكنهم يخشونه ويخافونه كل الخوف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement ‘I am the most God-fearing of you’ supports the distinction between security in God’s presence and fear of Him.
rows.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أنا أخشاكم لله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naml omits ‘except one who did wrong, then changed to good’ because that exception would make the assurance ‘you are among the secure’ incoherent.
rows.anchor: لا يحسن أن يقال: (إنك من الآمنين إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen’s confession of wrongdoing and submission with Solomon exemplifies changing from evil to good, so the exception and forgiveness fit Naml’s context.
rows.anchor: رب إني ظلمت نفسي وأسلمت مع سليمان لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He anticipates an apparent counterexample: Qasas also says Musa confessed his wrongdoing and God forgave him (28:16).
rows.anchor: وقد تقول: لقد ورد مثل هذا التعبير في سورة القصص أيضا وهو قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jann conveys quick motion and fear: it frightens people, and the serpent-like staff’s rapid movement suits the frightened scene.
rows.anchor: الجان دلالة الحركة السريعة، عصاه تهتز بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name jann is linked to concealment, in contrast to humans’ visibility.
rows.anchor: وسمي جان لأنه يستتر بمقابل الإنس (الإنس للظهور والجن للستر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although jinn are hidden, they can appear in forms; he cites the event involving Abu Hurayra to explain how one could see such a form.
rows.anchor: قد يظهر الجان بشكل أو يتشكل بشكل كما حدث مع أبو هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taha calls the staff a hayya to display God’s power and does not say Musa fled or panicked there.
rows.anchor: الحية جاءت في مكان واحد لبيان قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jann is chosen for Musa’s fear; thubaan is used before Pharaoh because one jann would not impress a crowd of hundreds and the scene calls for size and strength.
rows.anchor: لأنه مع الملأ الموجودين إذا كانوا مئات وتأتي بجان واحد ماذا يؤثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account uses thubaan twice before Pharaoh and jann twice with Musa, matching each term to its setting.
rows.anchor: ذكر ثعبان مرتين أمام فرعون وجان مرتين أمام موسى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say both occurred: water first burst abundantly, then diminished because of Israel’s sins; the author links the abundant term to praise in Baqarah and the lesser term to reproach in A‘raf.
rows.anchor: الماء انفجرت أولا بالماء الكثير ثم قل الماء بمعاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa is fa fasihah, signaling omitted but clear events: for example, ‘we said, strike the rock’ omits the actual striking before the water gushes.
rows.anchor: وهذه الفاء إذن هي فاء الفصيحة التي تدل على أن هناك محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other fa-fasihah examples include the omitted actions in 17:16 and in the command to Moses and Aaron to go to the people who denied them.
rows.anchor: وقد تكرر استخدام هذه الفاء في مواطن عديدة في القرآن الكريم منها

words: ثم تول عنهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Solomon’s story, the text omits the hoopoe taking the letter, carrying and dropping it by Bilqis, and waiting; the meaning remains clear.
rows.anchor: المفروض أن الهدهد أخذ الكتاب وذهب به وألقاه عند بلقيس وانتظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the ‘few numbered days’ wording by the absence of a preceding reminder of deeds and reckoning; when sins were recalled, they described them as fewer.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكروا بها قالوا أياما معدودات لأن الآثام التي ذكروا بها أقل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view is that one faction said ‘ayaman ma‘duda’ and another said ‘ayaman ma‘dudat.’
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول أن قسماً قالوا (أياماً معدودة) والقسم الآخر قال (أياماً معدودات)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He introduces Musa’s story in Naml and Qasas as another broad narrative comparison, to be studied through its many similarities and differences.
rows.anchor: ومثال آخر على التشابه والاختلاف في القرآن الكريم ما جاء في سورتي النمل والقصص

words: آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He introduces Luqman’s counsel as beginning with God’s gift of wisdom and the command to thank Him.
rows.anchor: تلك هي الوصية وقد بدأت بذكر إتيان لقمان الحكمة
